source.title: An integrative theory of locus coeruleus-norepinephrine function: adaptive gain and optimal performance.

confidence_rationale: The canonical theoretical framework for LC-NE as an exploration-exploitation controller, and the second pillar cited at MECH-440 adjudication (supports 0.78). It establishes the tonic/phasic LC dichotomy: phasic LC promotes exploitation of the current task, tonic LC promotes disengagement and a search for alternative behaviours (exploration), with ACC/OFC monitoring task utility and driving the mode. This grounds the 'tonic exploration floor whose level tracks the utility of the current policy' framing of MECH-440. It is a review/theory, not a causal experiment (Tervo 2014 provides the causal complement), so confidence is moderate and weighted toward conceptual mapping rather than primary evidence.
failure_signatures: Adaptive-gain theory describes tonic NE as raising responsivity/gain broadly (a global modulator), which is closer to a temperature/gain knob than to learned PER-PARAMETER state-conditioned weight noise; reading MECH-440's fine-grained sigma into a global gain signal risks over-claiming the biological specificity.

The theory is largely conceptual/modelling synthesis; the exploration claim is an interpretation of LC firing modes, and a global gain increase could in principle act like the non-propagating post-softmax temperature that V3-EXQ-687 already falsified, rather than the propagating weight noise MECH-440 requires.

Tonic-mode 'disengagement and search' is about ABANDONING the current task, which maps onto goal-disengagement / task-switching more than onto increasing the DIVERSITY of committed actions within a task -- a possible mis-mapping to the F-dominance ceiling.

mapping.source_claim_statement: LC neurons show two modes: phasic LC activation is driven by outcomes of task-related decisions and facilitates exploitation of the current task; tonic LC activity is associated with disengagement from the current task and search for alternative behaviours (exploration). ACC and OFC, which monitor task-related utility, are proposed to drive these LC modes to optimise utility over short and long timescales (adaptive gain).
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-440's tonic LC-NE exploration FLOOR is the standing, utility-tracking exploration drive that Aston-Jones & Cohen describe as the tonic mode: when the current policy's utility wanes, exploration should rise. This grounds the existence and utility-contingency of a tonic exploration floor and the role of ACC/OFC (the dACC/lPFC/OFC analogs in REE selection) in setting it -- the conceptual backbone for why a state-conditioned floor is the right object.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Adaptive gain is a GLOBAL responsivity/gain modulation, conceptually closer to a temperature/gain term than to learned per-parameter weight noise. MECH-313's already-falsified post-softmax temperature is itself a 'gain-like' construct, so Aston-Jones & Cohen support the FUNCTIONAL motivation (a utility-tracking tonic exploration drive) without endorsing the specific per-parameter, propagating-into-argmax implementation MECH-440 chose over the temperature route. It is a review/theory, not causal primary data.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical/integrative review of monkey LC-NE neurophysiology and computational modelling; no new causal perturbation data of its own.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high as a canonical theory review, but it is synthesis rather than primary causal data (Tervo 2014 carries the causal weight). Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds the tonic-floor FUNCTION strongly but the 'global gain' framing is closer to the temperature route MECH-440 explicitly rejected than to per-parameter weight noise. Transfer risk moderate (monkey LC theory -> RL selection head).
